sentences.text:
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned HCGP for respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2, who is served in the matter has remained unrepresented before this Court.
3.

FIR in Crime No.185/2024 was registered by Hosakote Police Station, Bengaluru, against petitioner herein for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information dated 07.06.2024 received from the victim girl aged about 17 years 11 months.
During the course of investigation of the case, petitioner herein was arrested on 10.06.2024 and remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation in the case is completed and NC: 2024:KHC:51316 charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences.
Bail application filed by him before the jurisdictional Sessions Court in Crl.Misc.No.1469/2024 was rejected on 16.07.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition has prayed to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition.

6. In the first information submitted by the victim girl, she has stated that in the year 2023, she got acquainted to the petitioner through Instagram Application and the petitioner had proposed to her.
Subsequently, on the promise of marrying her, petitioner allegedly had sexual intercourse with her against her wishes.

In the month of September, 2023, petitioner had come to her house when there was no body else in the house and with a promise to marry the victim girl, he had sexual intercourse with her in her house and subsequently, in the month of December, 2023 somebody informed over phone that petitioner is already married.
Thereafter, victim girl allegedly quarrelled with him and inspite of the same, petitioner promised to marry her and subsequently his phone was found NC:

sentences.text: On 05.06.2024, victim girl was taken to Hospital since she was suffering from pain in her waist.
Thereafter, she was admitted in the Hospital and she had given birth to a girl child.
It is in this background, she had approached the police.
Victim girl's statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. was recorded in the present case by the jurisdictional Magistrate on 19.06.2024.

In the said statement, victim girl has stated that after petitioner had promised to marry her, she had informed the same to her father and in turn her father had informed the parents of the petitioner about the said proposal.
Subsequently, petitioner came to their house and he was residing in their house for nearly a period of two months.
During the said time, relative of the victim girl who came to their house after seeing the petitioner informed the victim girl and her parents that the petitioner was already married.

Petitioner who had left the house of the victim girl in September,
2023 thereafter had not returned to their home.
On 04.06.2024, she had gone to the Hospital and thereafter delivered a girl child in the hospital.

A perusal of the averments made in the first information as well as in the statement of the victim girl under Section 164 of Cr.PC would reveal that NC: 2024:KHC:51316 petitioner and the victim girl were acquainted with each other and the petitioner was also staying in house of the victim girl and the father of the victim girl had proposed for the marriage of the petitioner with the victim girl.
According to the victim girl, petitioner had left her house in the month of September, 2023 and thereafter had not returned home.
Complaint is subsequently filed in the month of June, 2024.
Petitioner, who has no other criminal antecedents is in custody for the last nearly six months.
His confession statement would reveal that he was earlier married and his wife had died and thereafter, he got acquainted with the victim girl and they started to love each other.

Be that as it may, considering the fact that investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed and the trial in the case is yet to commence, wherein the prosecution has cited all together 27 charge sheet witnesses in the present case, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of regular bail needs to be answered affirmatively.

Accordingly, the following order:-
7. The petition is allowed.
The petitioner is directed to be enlarged on bail in Spl. Case No.604/2024 pending before the Court of Addl.
